The real projects carry no results and no quotes on purpose — no verified metrics exist for them, and inventing any would be worse than showing none.

en.title: A bail bond site built for the 2 a.m. search
en.summary: A mobile-first website for a Houston bail agency: one-tap calls, a one-minute release form, the jails it serves and payment plans — in English and Spanish.
en.challenge: Families search for a bail bondsman at 2 a.m., on a phone, and call whoever looks most trustworthy first. An outdated site loses that call.
en.solution: A fast site led by the 24/7 number: a one-minute release form, the county jails served, premiums and payment plans explained up front, reviews, a Spanish version and a chat that answers when the office cannot.

projects._note: In development. The screens are product designs shown with Ironwood Bail Bonds, a fictional agency; no agency uses it yet.

en.title: One system for the whole bail agency
en.summary: An agency portal and agent app for US bail bond companies — bonds, court dates, check-ins, e-signature and payments in one place.
en.challenge: Most bail agencies still run on paper files, a shared inbox and a spreadsheet of court dates. One missed hearing can cost the full bond.
en.solution: A portal for the office and an app for agents. Every bond, defendant and cosigner lives on one record; court-date reminders and check-ins go out by text in English and Spanish; cosigners sign and pay the premium from their phone. In development — shown here with a fictional agency.

en.title: A bilingual corporate site for a certified solar contractor
en.summary: EPC services, megawatt-scale installations and technical partnerships, in Arabic and English.
en.challenge: A certified solar and energy-storage contractor in Riyadh had to read as credible to industrial buyers in two languages — and turn that credibility into enquiries rather than admiration.
en.solution: A bilingual corporate site built around the evidence. The EPC services are stated plainly, the completed megawatt-scale rooftop and ground-mounted installations get a gallery of their own, and the certifications and technical partnerships — Huawei, Schneider Electric — sit where a buyer looks for them first. Every section routes to an enquiry.

projects._note: Cover and gallery are the product's marketing renders, cropped to 16:10. They are built from the app's own source with a demo tenant ("Marina Interiors"), so every name and number on them is demo data, and the case study says so.

en.title: A WhatsApp CRM that turns conversations into sales
en.summary: One shared inbox for the whole team, with an AI assistant, a sales pipeline, automations and broadcasts — all built around WhatsApp.
en.challenge: More than two billion people use WhatsApp, and plenty of businesses sell on it. But one phone, several staff and no record of who said what means leads go cold, customers wait, and nobody can see the pipeline.
en.solution: A complete business platform built around the company’s WhatsApp line. The team works every conversation from one shared inbox. An AI assistant answers from the company’s own knowledge base, qualifies the lead and hands it to a person at the right moment. Contacts, tags, deals and tasks live in one CRM; trigger-based automations route new leads and send follow-ups; broadcasts go out in bulk with delivery and read tracking; and a dashboard shows management what is happening today. The screens shown use a demo workspace, not a customer’s data.

en.title: A bilingual landing page for an ultra-premium compound
en.summary: Seven residence types, clubhouse facilities and neighbourhood highlights — all built around scheduling a visit.
en.challenge: An ultra-premium residential compound in Al Khobar needed one page that could carry its standard in both Arabic and English: seven residence types, the clubhouse, the neighbourhood — and end in a scheduled visit rather than a phone number at the bottom.
en.solution: A bilingual landing page with an English/Arabic toggle and full right-to-left support. Each residence type — apartments, town villas and executive villas — has its floor plan and specifications; the fifty-plus amenities are shown as a set rather than a list; the neighbourhood is placed by its landmarks. Schedule-a-visit and WhatsApp enquiry flows stay in reach the whole way down.

en.title: A booking website for luxury holiday homes in Dubai
en.summary: Holiday homes with Burj Khalifa and sea views, searched by date and party size and booked from one site.
en.challenge: A holiday-home operator in Dubai needed a website of its own, where guests can see each home and its views, check the dates and book the stay.
en.solution: An English booking website led by the views that sell the homes — the Burj Khalifa, the fountain and the sea. Guests search by arrival, departure, adults and children, browse each property with its amenities and gallery, and can book their stay from any page.

en.title: The main website for a Saudi marketing agency
en.summary: Services, portfolio, clients, official credentials and answers to real questions — the agency’s home online, in Arabic.
en.challenge: A marketing agency’s own website is the first thing its prospects judge it by. It had to present six service lines, the agency’s work and the registrations of a licensed Saudi business in one place.
en.solution: An Arabic company website built around proof: the service lines laid out one by one, the portfolio and client partners, the agency’s official registrations shown where a cautious buyer looks for them, answers to the questions prospects actually ask, and call and WhatsApp buttons that stay on screen.

en.title: A landing page for the agency’s real estate line
en.summary: The campaigns, landing pages, video and design the agency delivers for Saudi property companies — shown, not described.
en.challenge: Property buyers take longer to decide, and developers are wary of agencies. The agency needed a page that proves its real estate record rather than one that talks about it.
en.solution: A focused Arabic landing page that shows instead of claims: the property companies the agency works with, the ad platforms it runs campaigns on, real campaign screenshots with their figures as reported by the ad accounts, landing-page, video and design samples — and WhatsApp and call buttons at every step.

en.title: The landing page behind the agency’s own ads
en.summary: Where the agency’s paid campaigns send their traffic — built to turn a click into a consultation.
en.challenge: Paid traffic is expensive, and a visitor from an ad decides in seconds. The agency needed a page built for exactly that visitor.
en.solution: A fast Arabic landing page with one job. A clear headline and a free-consultation offer above the fold, the agency’s official credentials straight after, the platforms it works with — Google, Meta, Snapchat, TikTok, Salla and Zid — its client logos, six service lines, an FAQ written around real objections, and WhatsApp and call buttons fixed on screen. Light and dark themes included.

en.title: A landing page for the agency’s web development line
en.summary: A landing page for an agency’s web development line, written to turn visitors into qualified leads.
en.challenge: A Saudi digital marketing agency needed one page to sell a single service line — websites, online stores and landing pages — clearly enough that the lead arrives already knowing what it wants.
en.solution: A conversion-focused Arabic landing page: the services broken down so a visitor can see which one they need, trust signals and credentials placed exactly where the doubt appears, and WhatsApp and phone calls-to-action repeated down the page rather than parked at the bottom.

en.title: An AI legal assistant, available around the clock
en.summary: A legal assistant that answers questions about your rights, guides you through common legal issues and helps draft basic documents.
en.challenge: Ordinary legal questions — what your rights are, what a basic document needs to say — usually mean finding a lawyer first. Most people simply never ask them.
en.solution: A chat assistant built on a Hugging Face model with a knowledge base spanning several areas of law. It answers questions about rights and common legal situations and helps draft basic legal documents, in an interface anyone can use without being walked through it. Still in development.

en.title: Hotel search, booking and an admin panel
en.summary: A full-stack booking application: search with real-time availability, secure accounts, and an admin panel behind it.
en.challenge: A booking product has two sides that must stay in step — guests searching for what is actually free, and staff changing listings, rooms and reservations behind them.
en.solution: A MERN application with a REST API on Node and Express, JWT authentication for accounts, and a MongoDB layer with validation. Guests search against real-time availability; the admin panel manages listings, rooms and reservations against the same data, so the two sides can never drift apart.

projects._note: The client app is not published, so the showcase shows the real API source (assets/captures/lamabooking/). Add client screenshots here if the frontend is deployed.

en.title: Booking patients actually finish
en.summary: Online booking, shared patient records and SMS reminders for a dental group.
en.challenge: Phone-only booking, paper files and a 30% no-show rate.
en.solution: Online booking, a shared patient record across offices, and automated SMS reminders.

en.title: A broker app agents open 40 times a day
en.summary: Listings, leads and deal tracking for a brokerage's agents.
en.challenge: Leads lived in personal phones and were lost when agents left.
en.solution: A mobile app for agents and a dashboard for managers, with every lead owned by the company.

en.title: From a group text to one operations portal
en.summary: An operations portal, driver app and NetSuite sync for 11 depots.
en.challenge: Dispatch ran on a group text and three spreadsheets that only one person understood.
en.solution: Two weeks of discovery in the warehouses, then a portal, a driver app and an ERP sync shipped every two weeks.
